text: “那个男孩被伟大的风行者带走了。”查理抬起颤抖的手。“伊萨夸尼高兴时，或萨满召唤它的力量时，这灵体就会把人偷走，迫使他们跟着它在空中奔跑，速度快到脚都被烧掉！然后，伟大的风行者会赐给你一双和它一样的脚。你会变成吃人的怪物。
“如果那个男孩回来，他会……变得不同。他的心会像冰一样冷。除非那颗心先融化，否则他不会死。”
查理的故事让你想起很久以前听过的一件事。这个故事荒诞无比；然而，从她热切的眼神中，你看得出她深信不疑。

en.title: Alone Against the Frost · 73
text: “The boy was taken by the Great Wind-Walker.” Charlie raises a trembling hand. “When it pleases Ithakwanni, or when a shaman summons its power, the spirit steals you away; forces you to run with it across the sky so fast that your feet burn off! Then, the Great Wind-Walker gives you feet like its own. You become a creature who eats human flesh.
“If the boy comes back, he will be… different. Changed. His heart will be ice. He will not die unless that heart is first melted.”
Charlie’s tale echoes something you heard long ago. The story is fantastic—yet from her fervid eyes, it is plain she utterly believes it.
